_comment: CAVE BIOME VARIETY. Vanilla picks underground biomes by NEAREST box, not containment: dripstone_caves is continentalness >= 0.8 and lush_caves is humidity >= 0.7, so dripstone wins wherever C > H + 0.1. Terra Continental's radial bumps push inland continentalness to ~1.48 (vanilla tops out near 1.0) while humidity keeps its normal range (max ~0.62), so dripstone won almost everywhere underground - only ~8% of land is actually inside its band. The old continent_inland_stretch fix is inert under Tectonic because it hangs off minecraft:overworld/continents, which Tectonic does not use for biome climate. This file is the biome-only hook: Tectonic's version is literally add(full_continents, 0), and full_continents itself must NOT be overridden because initial_density_without_jaggedness, sloped_cheese, roughness and factor/islands all read it - changing it would reshape terrain. The compression is blended in by DEPTH (via terra_continental:depth, which follows the terrain rather than cutting a flat plane through mountains) so it is inactive at the surface: surface biomes and terrain are untouched, and only the cave bands see the compressed range. Blend is 0 at depth 0.1 and full by depth 0.3; underground biomes live at depth 0.2-0.9. SHORE BIOMES ONLY AT THE SHORE: argument1 is terra_continental:shape/continents_biome, Tectonic's full_continents lifted to at least -0.1 (out of vanilla's coast band, -0.19 to -0.11) where the ground's offset passes 0.05 -> 0.12 (about +20 -> +50). The coast remap raises mountains on ground whose biome continentalness is still in the coast band, and vanilla's coast slice at low erosion is stony_shore: the user's flight (2026-10-25) found flat Stony Shore at y ~213 in the south-coast mountains. 2-D and biome selection only (terrain reads full_continents and shape/continents, never this router entry); the cave compression below still reads the unlifted value. Generated by preview/shape_pack.py (high_coast_biomes).
